docs.text: Architecture Overview StudErn uses a classic client-server architecture with a RESTful API. System Components Frontend: React + Vite single-page application. Backend: Laravel API with JWT-based authentication. Database: SQLite (local) or MySQL (production-ready). Queue: Laravel queue with database driver for local development. Data Flow The frontend authenticates the user and stores a JWT token. API requests include the token to access protected endpoints. The backend validates the token, authorizes the user, and returns data. Some actions (such as job posting payments) trigger payment flows and queue jobs. Layered View Presentation: React components, routes, and contexts API Layer: Laravel controllers and request validation Domain Layer: Services for hiring and payments Persistence: Eloquent models and database tables Async: Queue workers for background processing Integrations Payment gateway (bKash) for paid postings JWT device validation for session security Key Domain Areas Companies and company memberships Hiring details (jobs and internships) Payments and free-posting logic Applications and interviews Technology Decisions Laravel provides rapid development and a stable ecosystem. React + Vite offers fast iteration and modern UI patterns. Database queue driver ensures reliable background work in local environments.

docs.text: Company APIs Company endpoints manage organizations, members, and privileges. Core Flows Create a company Add users to the company Manage company-level privileges Maintain company links Membership & Privileges Users must belong to a company to manage hiring Privileges are stored in company_user_privileges Common privileges: can_post_jobs, can_manage_jobs, can_manage_users Key Endpoints POST /api/companies Create a company GET /api/companies/my List companies for the authenticated user POST /api/companies/{companyId}/users Add a user to a company GET /api/companies/{companyId}/users List users in a company POST /api/companies/{companyId}/users/{userId}/privileges Grant or revoke company privileges POST /api/companies/{companyId}/links Add a company link Permissions Most endpoints require company membership. Managing users or privileges typically requires can_manage_users or admin privilege. Example: Create Company Request: { "name": "Tech Solutions Inc", "address": "Dhaka, Bangladesh", "website": "https://example.com" } Response: { "status": "success", "message": "Company created successfully", "data": { "id": 12, "name": "Tech Solutions Inc" } } See studern-backend/.wiki/Company for detailed request and response examples.

docs.text: Hiring APIs Hiring endpoints support both job and internship postings with shared metadata and type-specific detail objects. Core Endpoints POST /api/companies/{companyId}/hiring GET /api/companies/{companyId}/hiring GET /api/companies/{companyId}/hiring/{hiringDetailId} PUT /api/companies/{companyId}/hiring/{hiringDetailId} DELETE /api/companies/{companyId}/hiring/{hiringDetailId} Public browse endpoints: GET /api/hiring/browse GET /api/hirings/{id} Payload Structure (Create) Top-level fields: job_title hiring_type (job | internship) work_from (remote | onsite | hybrid) employment_type (full-time | part-time | contract | temporary | freelance) num_of_openings description closing_at Server-managed: posted_at is set by the backend at creation time Job details (when hiring_type is job): payment_type min_salary / max_salary currency perks[] pay_per timeline experience_year Internship details (when hiring_type is internship): min_stipend / max_stipend currency pay_per duration_weeks / duration_months perks[] when_to_start start_date_from / start_date_to Work from details: work_from_type timezone (remote) work_start_time / work_end_time (remote) days_in_office_per_week (hybrid) only_from_office_location Permissions User must be a company member with can_post_jobs to create Update/delete requires can_manage_jobs or admin Payment Gating First posting is free Subsequent postings require a payment package Supported packages: Basic Standard Premium Paid posting request example: { "job_title": "Frontend Developer", "hiring_type": "job", "work_from": "remote", "employment_type": "full-time", "num_of_openings": 1, "description": "Build UI features", "closing_at": "2026-03-20T23:59:59Z", "payment_package": "Standard", "job_details": { "payment_type": "fixed_pay", "min_salary": 45000, "max_salary": 65000, "pay_per": "month" }, "work_from_details": { "work_from_type": "remote", "timezone": "Asia/Dhaka", "work_start_time": "09:00", "work_end_time": "17:00" } } Paid response (payment initiated): { "status": "success", "message": "Payment initiated", "data": { "payment": { "id": 45, "amount": 4500, "status": "pending" }, "bkash_url": "https://checkout.bkash.com/...", "requires_payment": true } } For full payload examples and validation rules, see studern-backend/.wiki/Hiring.

docs.text: Backend Overview The StudErn backend is a Laravel API that powers authentication, authorization, hiring workflows, and payment processing. Architecture Snapshot Framework: Laravel Auth: JWT with optional device payload validation Data: Eloquent models backed by SQLite/MySQL Async: Laravel queues (database driver recommended for local dev) Core Concepts Authentication : JWT tokens are required for protected routes. Authorization : Company membership and privilege checks gate company actions. Hiring : Jobs and internships share a unified hiring_details model with type-specific details. Payments : A free-posting rule with package-based paid upgrades. Key Modules Auth : login, registration, verification, password reset Companies : creation, membership, privileges, links Hiring : create, browse, update, delete, and public browse Payments : gateway integration and package logic Queue : background work, retries, and failed jobs Request & Response Conventions JSON requests with Authorization header for protected routes Standard response envelope: status, message, data/messages Validation errors return messages per field API Structure Routes live in routes/api.php and are grouped into: Public : welcome, browse listings Protected : company, hiring, payments Admin : privilege management and system operations

docs.text: Payments StudErn includes a modular payment system for job posting and other paid modules. Overview One free job posting per user Paid packages required after the free posting is used Payments are tracked in payments and payment_gateways tables Data Model payment_gateways: gateway configuration payments: transaction records Job Posting Payment Flow User starts a job posting Backend checks free posting eligibility If paid, the system initiates a gateway payment Gateway callback completes the payment Job becomes active after successful payment Payment Packages Basic (BDT 3,850) Standard (BDT 4,500) Premium (BDT 5,300) Key Endpoints POST /api/payments/initiate POST /api/payments/callback GET /api/payments/packages?module_type=job_posting Example: Initiate Payment { "module_type": "job_posting", "module_id": 123, "package_name": "Basic", "callback_url": "https://studern.com/api/payments/callback" } Example response: { "status": "success", "message": "Payment initiated successfully", "data": { "payment": { "id": 456, "amount": 3850, "status": "pending" }, "bkash_url": "https://checkout.bkash.com/..." } } Example: Callback { "paymentID": "BKASH_PAYMENT_ID", "status": "success", "trxID": "BKASH_TRANSACTION_ID" } Gateways bKash tokenized checkout is supported Gateway configuration is stored in payment_gateways Configuration Typical environment variables: BKASH_BASE_URL BKASH_APP_KEY BKASH_APP_SECRET BKASH_USERNAME BKASH_PASSWORD See studern-backend/.wiki/Payment for detailed reference, configuration, and examples.

docs.text: Queue Processing StudErn uses Laravel queues for asynchronous tasks. Recommended Driver for Local Dev database (set QUEUE_CONNECTION=database) Why Database Driver No external services required Stable local development experience Transparent job storage in the database Common Tasks Start a worker: php artisan queue:work Listen mode (dev only): php artisan queue:listen Inspect failed jobs: php artisan queue:failed Retry failed jobs: php artisan queue:retry all Tables Used jobs failed_jobs job_batches Operational Notes Use queue:work for production-style processing. Use queue:listen for quick local feedback. Tune retry behavior with --tries and --timeout flags.

docs.text: Authentication Endpoints This section summarizes the authentication endpoints documented in the backend wiki. Login POST /api/login Purpose: - Authenticate via email or phone and return a JWT. Key fields: - identifier (email or phone) - password - devicePayload (recommended) - timezone - screen - platform - ua Validation notes: identifier must map to a verified contact password is validated against stored hash Example request: { "identifier": "john.doe@example.com", "password": "SecurePass123!", "devicePayload": { "timezone": "Asia/Dhaka", "screen": "1920x1080", "platform": "Win32", "ua": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)" } } Example success response: { "status": "success", "message": "Login successful.", "data": { "token": "<jwt>", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "user": { "id": 1, "firstname": "John", "lastname": "Doe" } } } Token Refresh POST /api/refresh Purpose: - Issue a new token from a valid existing token. Notes: Requires a valid token in Authorization header Example curl: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/refresh \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" Logout POST /api/logout Purpose: - Invalidate the current token. Notes: Token is blacklisted server-side Example curl: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/logout \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" Registration POST /api/register Purpose: - Create a new user account and begin verification. Common fields: firstname, lastname contact (email or phone) password Contact Verification POST /api/contact-verification POST /api/contact-verification/resend Purpose: - Verify email or phone for account activation. Notes: Verification token is required Password Reset POST /api/reset-password/request POST /api/reset-password/verify POST /api/reset-password/reset Purpose: - Request, verify, and complete password resets. Common fields: contact reset token new password Common Responses 200 OK for success 401 Unauthorized for invalid credentials or tokens 422 Unprocessable Entity for validation failures For detailed payloads and examples, refer to the backend wiki files under studern-backend/.wiki/auth.

docs.text: JWT Authentication StudErn uses JWT for API authentication. The client sends a token with each protected request. Flow User logs in using /api/login. The backend returns a JWT token. The frontend stores the token and attaches it to requests. The backend validates the token and applies device validation. Device Validation The middleware checks device payload when provided. Missing device payload is allowed but results in a skip of device validation. Common Responses 401 Unauthorized when token is missing or expired. 403 Forbidden when user lacks a required privilege. Related Docs Overview: auth/overview.md Endpoints: auth/endpoints.md

docs.text: Authentication Overview StudErn uses JWT-based authentication with optional device fingerprint validation. JWT Basics Tokens are issued during login and sent with every protected request. The token is passed in the Authorization header: Authorization: Bearer Tokens expire and can be refreshed using the refresh endpoint. Device Payload For security, authenticated requests can include a devicePayload in the request body. This enables device-based session validation. Recommended fields: timezone screen platform ua Note: Some endpoints accept requests without devicePayload, but providing it improves security and session tracking. Authorization & Privileges Company actions require company membership and specific privileges (e.g., can_post_jobs). Admin endpoints require elevated privileges (e.g., manage_privileges_of_users). Related Pages Endpoint details: auth/endpoints.md

docs.text: API Integration The frontend talks to the backend API through axios. Base URL Configured using VITE_API_BASE_URL Defaults to http://localhost:8000/api Error Handling API responses map to success/error objects Validation errors surface as field messages Authentication JWT tokens are required for protected endpoints Token is attached to each request via axios default headers AuthContext clears tokens on 401 responses Device Payload Login requests include devicePayload for backend device validation Payload is generated from browser timezone, screen, platform, and user agent Error Mapping Validation errors (422) are converted into field-level messages Generic errors map to a fallback message for the UI Example: Authenticated Request import axios from 'axios'; const API_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:8000/api'; export const fetchCompanies = async () => { const response = await axios.get(`${API_BASE}/companies/my`); return response.data.data; };

docs.text: Frontend Auth Flow The frontend handles authentication through AuthContext and JWT storage. Login Sequence User submits identifier and password. AuthContext sends POST /api/login with devicePayload. On success, token and user are stored in localStorage. Axios Authorization header is set for future requests. User privileges are fetched. Example login payload: { "identifier": "john.doe@example.com", "password": "SecurePass123!", "devicePayload": { "timezone": "Asia/Dhaka", "screen": "1920x1080", "platform": "Win32", "ua": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)" } } Logout Sequence Frontend calls POST /api/logout. Token and user data are cleared from storage. Authorization header is removed. Token Expiration Axios response interceptor clears auth state on 401. UI redirects to login when unauthenticated. Contact Verification Signup initiates verification flow. Verify contact pages handle OTP or email verification.

docs.text: Local Development Use this page to set up the backend and frontend on a local machine. Backend Setup Install dependencies: Run composer install in studern-backend. Copy environment file: Duplicate .env.example to .env if needed. Configure the database: SQLite is supported out-of-the-box. Run migrations: php artisan migrate (Optional) Seed data: php artisan db:seed Start the API server: php artisan serve Queue Setup (Local) Set QUEUE_CONNECTION=database in .env Run queue migrations if needed: php artisan queue:table php artisan migrate Start a worker: php artisan queue:work Frontend Setup Install dependencies: Run npm install in studern-frontend. Configure API base URL: Set VITE_API_BASE_URL in the frontend .env if needed. Start the dev server: npm run dev Default URLs Backend API: http://localhost:8000/api Frontend: http://localhost:5173 Common Issues Authentication failures usually come from missing or expired JWT tokens. Posting jobs may require a payment package after the free posting is used. Queue processing depends on QUEUE_CONNECTION (database is recommended for local dev).

docs.text: Getting Started This guide helps you run the StudErn backend and frontend locally. Prerequisites PHP 8.3+ Composer Node.js 18+ npm SQLite or MySQL (the repository currently uses SQLite by default) Repositories StudErn is split into two main applications: Backend: Laravel API in studern-backend Frontend: React + Vite in studern-frontend High-Level Steps Install dependencies for both projects. Configure environment variables for backend and frontend. Run migrations and seed data as needed. Start the backend API. Start the frontend dev server. Environment Basics Backend uses .env for database and queue configuration. Frontend uses VITE_API_BASE_URL to point to the API. For local development, database queue is recommended. Continue to local-development.md for detailed steps.
